AGENDA
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MAY 14, 2025

  SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:00 PM

  Linda Lopez, Chair
  Kim Apodaca, Vice Chair
  Rosa Barragan, Planning Commissioner
  Chris Macias, Planning Commissioner
  Lisa Vernola-Salas, Planning Commissioner

Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to
the Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to
a vote. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
future Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when
services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or
service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.
 CALL TO ORDER

FLAG SALUTE

Commissioner Vernola-Salas

ROLL CALL OF MEMBERS

MINUTES

1.  MEETING MINUTES
  Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve the minutes of the Special Planning
  Commission meeting of April 23, 2025.

PUBLIC HEARING

2.  Director Approval Request No. 2025-04 to permit the sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption (Type
  41 ABC license) in an existing 1,400 square foot bona fide restaurant located within an approximately
  1.39-acre commercial shopping center. The subject site is located at 12227 Norwalk Boulevard (APN:
  8024-024-023). Environmental: Consider and find that the proposed use is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).
  That the Planning Commission:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. 25-07 to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2025-04 subject to the
  Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
  2. Find that the proposed use is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines
  pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I, Alexander Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development/Secretary, hereby certify that the foregoing
agenda was posted at City Hall not less than 72-hours prior to the meeting and forwarded to each member of
the Norwalk Planning Commission on May 8, 2025.

Alexander Hamilton
Interim Planning Commission Secretary

   MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  APRIL 23, 2025

The meeting was called to order by Chair Lopez at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Barragan, Commissioner Macias, Vice Chair Apodaca, and Chair Lopez.
Commissioner Vernola-Salas was absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Interim
Director of Community Development; Araceli Almazan, Deputy City Attorney; Gabriel R.
Salazar, Senior Planner; Carlos Rojas, Senior Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann,
Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meeting of March 26, 2025.

CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP) NO. 2024-01
PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN (PDP) NO. 2024-02
TENTATIVE TRACT MAP (TTM) NO. 084624
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST (DAR) NO. 2025-05
Johanna Crooker of MLC Holdings, Inc. (“Applicant”); a request to redevelop and
subdivide a 4.5-acre site currently occupied by a 53,450 square foot bowling alley and
retail tenant spaces into a mixed-use development composed of 83 three-story
townhomes and 10 three-story live-work units, landscaping improvements, and
associated infrastructure on a 4.5-acre lot located at 11459 Imperial Highway (also known
as Assessor’s Parcel Number (“APN”) 8023-008-004) in the General Commercial (C-3)
Zone.
Environmental: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project
will not have a significant effect on the environment per Section 15332 (In-Fill
Development Projects) of the CEQA Guidelines. Section 15332 involves in-fill
development within urbanized areas.
The project includes a request for:
(1) CUP: To permit a mixed-use development in the C-3 Zone;
(2) PDP: To permit the construction of a three-story mixed-use development and
  associated site improvements;
(3) TTM: To subdivide the lot into a condominium tract map; and
(4) DAR: To permit a new wall/fence within the front setback area along Gettysburg Drive.

Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Senior Planner Salazar
presented a detailed report stating that, currently, the site is occupied by a 53,450 square
foot bowling alley and retail tenant spaces; that the applicant proposes to redevelop and
subdivide the 4.5 acre site into a mixed-use development composed of 83 three-story
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 23, 2025

townhomes and 10 three-story live-work units; that Meritage Homes held a community
meeting on January 30, 2025, which was attended by about twenty-three residents who
raised concerns about privacy and wall height abutting the single-family homes, noise,
demolition and construction hours, displacement, possible traffic issues, and vermin
infestation; that the applicant responded to these concerns by providing opaque windows
on the third story; and a six-foot high block wall with landscaping to create a buffer; that
the project site will be fumigated prior to demolition; and that construction hours will take
place between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. Monday through Friday; and that primary access
to the site will be through Imperial Highway.

Continuing with his presentation, Mr. Salazar shared that the project will have a positive
impact to the surrounding neighborhood, redevelop an existing commercial site into
housing, diversify housing stock, and improve the economic vitality of the site; that the
development complies with applicable city codes; that with the recommended conditions
of approval, provides adequate parking, vehicular circulation and pedestrian access; and
that it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning Commission approve the project.

Vice Chair Apodaca asked for clarification on the comment about displacement made by
residents at the community meeting, Senior Planner Salazar indicated that they referred
to gentrification, and that the homes would not be affordable for Norwalk residents.

In response to Vice Chair Apodaca’s comment on how did they come up with a
justification in parking by basically limiting two cars per unit, Mr. Salazar indicated that the
applicant provided a parking study that uses parking generation demand based on the
Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE) Parking Generation Manual sixth edition
(2021) and the Urban Land Institute’s Shared Parking, third edition (2020) manual. In
addition, the conditions of approval provide that Conditions, Covenants and Restrictions
(CC & R’s) of the homeowners’ association be complied with.

Commissioner Barragan commented on the importance of parking enforcement and
making sure that it is monitored. Mr. Salazar indicated that the CC & R’s include language
to this effect, and that the final tract map must be approved by the City Council.

Commissioner Macias commented on the 30 guest parking spaces, and he stated that
hopefully, the residents will not invite guests every day; and that regarding a corner unit
with a balcony, that consideration be given to providing some privacy for that homeowner.

The applicant, Johanna Crooker, Meritage Homes, stated that she would like to thank
staff for their professionalism and for being very responsive in getting them through this
process; that as staff provided a detailed report, she is going to focus on a few different
subjects; that Meritage Homes are the fifth largest home builder in the country; that they
have been around since 1985; that they have built almost over 200,000 homes across
the country; that they are a very experienced home builder; that they have built similar
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 3
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 23, 2025

townhomes in other communities; that they are very familiar with some of the parking
issues that come along with this level of density of development; that in the industry they
are known as the energy leaders; that they take a lot of pride in their developments; that
for the past eleven years their firm has received an award for being the Energy Star
Partner of the year; that they have won awards for surveys dealing with homebuyers
customer satisfaction; that they have also won awards for philanthropy in communities
that they work in; and that they decided to focus on meeting the needs for first-time
homebuyers with homes that are compatible with the surrounding neighborhood.

Continuing with her presentation, Ms. Crooker shared that after they put together their
development package, they reached out to the neighborhood by sending out 609 mailers;
that the flyer included a site plan as well as frequently asked questions; that on January
30, 2025 they had a community meeting at the Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex; that
they counted about 40 attendees, which included family members; that their design team
was in attendance to answer residents’ questions; that they asked residents to fill out
comment cards with a list of some of their concerns; that the comments received were on
the gentrification issue and parking; that they were asked to close off the access to
Gettysburg Drive; that a block wall was proposed at the northerly boundary, however,
they had a discussion with staff on possibly using tubular steel instead as long as it
achieves the goal that the neighbors were looking for, which is preventing access; that
they are open to both scenarios; that there were some requests to increase the existing
six-foot high wall, which is the maximum height permitted, but that they would be
amenable to increasing the height; that on the side elevation, they are proposing to make
the windows on the second floor and third floor opaque; that the current wall has a lot of
vegetation growing over it; that they can plant a hedge; that they are planning to
strategically place trees as well to block windows that will be facing those neighbors; and
that they can work with the neighbors, which they have done on other projects.

Ms. Crooker shared that traffic is another concern brought up in regards to the limited
ability to turn out of the driveway in that people would cut through the neighborhood; that
other issues dealt with construction, the timing of it, how long is it going to last, the noise,
the dust and vermin infestation that might scatter into the neighborhood; that as far as
timing, they will notify the neighbors beforehand, especially the demolition part of it; that
as far as the demolition and dust, the Air Quality Management District has a lot of very
stringent rules that they have to comply with; that they will be complying with the city’s
noise ordinance; that they will have pest control conduct remediation measures before
they demolish the building; that the residents also brought up questions regarding the
design of the commercial part of the building; that this is intended more for service
providers, such as hair stylists, photographers, certified public accountants, or real estate
agents; that another question was how would the commercial uses impact parking in the
neighborhood. Ms. Crooker provided slides showing the proposed development, the
transition from the commercial uses on the corner and transition to the blend of
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 4
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 23, 2025

commercial and residential; and she stated that the parking spaces in front are dedicated
during business hours to the live-work units.

Irma Ramos stated that she is a long-time Norwalk resident; that she is also a member of
a grass roots movement which is dedicated to bringing an equitable community to all the
residents of Norwalk; that she would like to express her opposition to this project; that she
attended the community meeting hosted by the developer; that she had one question;
that in light of the fact that they are taking away a community space, how does this project
benefit the residents of Norwalk; that she did not get a single good answer; that Keystone
Lanes is one of the very few entertainment venues left in Norwalk; that its loss will be felt;
that when she attended Norwalk High School, they held dances and fundraisers at that
facility; that they are replacing this with homes that are not affordable for its residents;
that the Norwalk first-time home buyers program offered its residents caps the total cost
at $125,000; that these homes will not qualify for that; that the applicant is trying to have
this project exempted from the California Environmental Quality Act by justifying it using
an inherent flawed traffic guide; that this matter was brought up previously by union
members; that determining the traffic numbers based on a flawed guide means that the
traffic numbers are flawed; that they are dumping traffic directly onto a major intersection;
and that they are concerned about accidents and increased traffic.

In response to Chair Lopez’ question if the applicant would like to make a rebuttal
statement, Traffic Engineer Charlene So, Urban Crossroads Inc., stated that they
prepared the trip generation assessment for the project; that she would like to address
the comment just made about the traffic; that the way the trip generation is done if there
is a pre-existing use on it, or allowed use, versus what is being proposed, they do a
comparison; that they did take a traffic count for the driveway for the existing use when it
was operational; that they did collect data from that which they compared against what
the trip generation would be for the proposed project; that they found that the bowling
alley retail use of the site generates about 754 daily two-way trips in comparison to the
proposed project which generates 596 trips; and that, basically, the development of the
proposed project results in a net reduction in traffic.

Commissioner Macias asked for clarification on the entrance to the property coming from
the west. Ms. So indicated that they would have to make a U-turn as she believes that
there is no left-turn lane onto the site. Commissioner Macias asked if there was any
proposal to provide an offset at the entrance similar to what buses use. Ms. So stated
that she does not believe that the site design allows for that.

Since there were no other comments, Chair Lopez closed the public hearing.

Commissioner Barragan stated that all of her questions have been answered. She
thanked Ms. Ramos for expressing her concerns and for attending tonight’s meeting; and
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 5
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 23, 2025

she added that she, too, shares her concerns with the affordability of housing. Further,
Commissioner Barragan thanked the builder for addressing the environmental concerns.

Commissioner Macias stated that he really appreciates the feedback on what the
residents asked for, and for the applicant complying by trying to come up with a solution.

Vice Chair Apodaca thanked Ms. Ramos for attending tonight and sharing her concerns.
She stated that she, too, went to that bowling alley since she was little and attended
bowling classes in 1985; that the facility has not been able to keep up with the
maintenance and what is required to maintain a state-of-the-art bowling alley; that she
totally understands Ms. Ramos’ concern; however, this project is going to increase the
beautification of the area; that she likes the appearance of the building and the design;
that she does not know if it will impact the traffic that much as the residents are going to
work in the morning and are coming back in the evening; that she believes the
development is going to be an improvement to the area, and that she will be looking
forward to seeing that project come to fruition.

Chair Lopez stated that it is a nice project; that it will provide a lot of homes for people in
need of housing; and she thanked everyone involved for their hard work.

It was moved by Vice Chair Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Barragan to: (1)
Adopt Resolution No. 25-03 to approve Conditional Use Permit No. 2024-01 subject to
the conditions of approval contained in respective Exhibit “A”; (2) Adopt Resolution No.
25-04 to approve Precise Development Plan No. 2024-02 subject to the conditions of
approval contained in respective Exhibit “A”; (3) Adopt Resolution No. 25-05 to approve
Tentative Tract Map No. 084624 subject to the conditions of approval contained in
respective Exhibit “A”; (4) Adopt Resolution No. 25-06 to approve Director Approval
Request No. 2025-05 subject to the conditions of approval contained in respective Exhibit
“A”; and (5) Consider and find that the proposed project is exempt from CEQA pursuant
to Section 15332 (In-fill Development Projects).

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Commissioner Barragan, Commissioner Macias, Vice Chair Apodaca,
  and Chair Lopez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Commissioner Vernola-Salas

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were no persons wishing to address the Planning Commission.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 6
Minutes of the Special Meeting  April 23, 2025

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 7:58 p.m.

  ________________________________
  LINDA LOPEZ, CHAIR

NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
   Planning Commission
  Agenda Report
  May 14, 2025

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development
  Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager

BY:  Matthew Morales, Planning Intern

SUBJECT:  Director Approval Request No. 2025-04 to allow the sale of beer and wine for on-
  site consumption (Type 41 ABC license) in an existing 1,400 square foot bona fide
  restaurant located within an approximately 1.39-acre commercial shopping center.
  Subject Site: 12227 Norwalk Boulevard (APN: 8024-024-023).
  Environmental: Consider and find that the proposed use is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing
  Facilities).

Recommendation:

That the Planning Commission:
1. Adopt Resolution No. 25-07 to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2025-04 subject to
the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
2. Find that the proposed use is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
Guidelines pursuant to Section 15301 (Existing Facilities).
Authority:

Section 17.02.203.B of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the Director of Community
Development (“Director”) to permit the on-sale alcohol sales within bona fide restaurants as defined
in NMC Section 17.04.140. The Director may at his or her discretion refer any request to the
Planning Commission for review and determination.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  May 14, 2025
  Page No. 2

Background:

The subject site, located at 12227 Norwalk Boulevard, is located within an existing 1.39-acre
commercial shopping center, more commonly known as Paddison Square, at the southwest corner
of Norwalk Boulevard and Crewe Street in the General Commercial (C-3) zone with a General Plan
land use designation of General Commercial.

Per Los Angeles County Assessor records, the multi-tenant commercial building was constructed
in 1968 and is approximately 19,800± square feet (SF) in size. The Norwalk Taco Factory is a
permitted “by-right” restaurant use within the subject tenant space and C-3 Zoning district in which
the property is located in.
The subject property is located within a fully developed area and surrounded by Single-Family
Residential (R-1) zone to the north and east and General Commercial (C-3) zone to the south and
west.
Request:

The applicant is requesting approval to allow the on-site sale and consumption of beer and wine
under a Type 41 State of California Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) license within an
approximately 1,400 SF bona fide restaurant (Norwalk Taco Factory). Norwalk Taco Factory will be
open daily. As part of the project, the applicant is proposing the following hours of operation:
  •  Monday through Sunday from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
The sale of alcohol is proposed to begin at 11:00 a.m. and end 60 minutes before closing time at
7:00 p.m.

There are no tenant improvement plans proposed for the existing, active bona fide food
establishment. The layout of the dining area shall remain the same (see Attachment C for existing
restaurant layout). The Norwalk Taco Factory is intending to complement its food selection by
offering a range of beer options to dine-in customers. Alcohol beverages are proposed to be stored
in an existing cooler used for bottled drinks. The operating restaurant currently has a total of 13
employees, with five (5) to six (6) employees per shift.
Analysis:

Subject Site Conditions Relating to Alcohol Sales
The following information is for Planning Commission consideration: 1) concentration of on-site
alcohol sales establishments, 2) neighborhood crime statistics, and 3) other alcohol establishments
within a quarter mile radius:

1. Concentration of on-site alcohol sales establishments – The request is to establish beer and wine
sales for on-site consumption at an existing restaurant within Census Tract No. 5553. The ABC
issues Type 41 licenses for on-sale beer and wine, which allows for the sale of beer and wine for
on-site consumption at the premises where sold. In this case, minors are allowed on the premises.
Currently, there are six (6) active on-sale alcohol establishments within Census Tract No. 5553 and
 Norwalk Planning Commission  May 14, 2025
  Page No. 3

ABC does not recommend more than four (4) on-sale licenses within this census tract. The proposal
would increase the number of establishments with on-sale licenses from six (6) to seven (7), which
will be above the maximum concentration threshold.

However, staff believes that the proposed use will contribute to the long-term economic
development goals of the City, provide an overall positive upgrade in the area and City through the
aesthetic character and ambiance of the proposed use, and result in an increase in business
taxes. Generally, beer and wine are expected offerings for restaurants such as the Taco Factory
and their beverage offerings will be enhanced.

The following is a table listing of all on-site alcohol sales establishments within Census Tract No.
5553:

  Existing On-Sale Alcohol Establishments Within Census Tract No. 5553
  No.  Business Name  Address  License Type
  1  El Taco Locco  12341 Imperial Hwy, Norwalk  41
  2  So Cal Pizza  12253 Imperial Hwy, Norwalk  41
  3  Applebee’s Neighborhood  12129 Imperial Hwy, Norwalk  47
  Grill and Bar
  4  Kung Pao Bowl  12331-12335  Imperial  Hwy,  41
  Norwalk
  5  Mountain Mike’s Pizza  12539 Imperial Hwy, Ste. 102,  41
  Norwalk
  6  California Fish Grill  12539 Imperial Hwy, Ste. 101  41
  Norwalk

2. Neighborhood crime statistics – The subject site is located within the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department Reporting District No. 0452. According to a report issued by ABC, the number of Part
1 crime incidents (Part I crimes are defined by the Federal Government as criminal homicide, rape,
robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny, theft, grand theft auto, and arson) was 157 in the
2024 crime dataset. The City of Norwalk’s district average is 69.5, and a high crime district is any
area with 20% above average Part I crime rate. Therefore, the reporting district in which Norwalk
Taco Factory proposes the sale of alcohol for on-site consumption is considered a high-crime
reporting district. However, staff findings indicate the proposed use to provide a net positive to the
City through economic benefit, opportunity, and ambiance.

3. Alcohol establishments within a quarter mile radius – The subject site is located at the southwest
 Norwalk Planning Commission  May 14, 2025
  Page No. 4

corner of Norwalk Boulevard and Crewe Street. Within a quarter mile radius of the subject site, there
are four (4) establishments with an on-site alcohol beverage license and three (3) establishments
with an off-site alcohol beverage license for the consumption of beer, wine or distilled spirits.
In consideration of the current activity related to the site and proximity of surrounding uses, staff
recommends approval with conditions that address the following issues:
  •  Limiting hours of operation;
  •  Providing surveillance system and lighting for the site; and
  •  Training and education for employees regarding alcohol sales.
The sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption within the bona fide restaurant is consistent with
the General Plan’s policies related to the General Commercial Land Use category. The project
encourages economic growth of a local business and enhancement of a commercial center, which
is important for providing adequate local-serving commercial uses.

Off-Street Parking and Site Circulation
The proposed on-site sale of beer and wine is ancillary to the existing bona fide restaurant and does
not intensify off-street parking requirements. Additionally, the existing floor area, at 1,400 square
feet is not proposed to be intensified. As such, additional off-street parking spaces are not required
as part of the proposed use.

Public Notification:

Public hearing notices were published in the Norwalk Patriot on May 2, 2025, and posted at locations
set forth in NMC Section 1.08.030 as well as mailed to 103 property owners within 500 feet of the
property. As of the writing of this report, staff has not received any correspondence regarding the
proposed project.
Environmental Assessment:

Pursuant to CEQA, this project will not have a significant effect on the environment per Section
15301 (Existing Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines. Section 15301 Class 1 consists of operation,
repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing or minor alteration of existing public or private
structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no
expansion of existing use. The project involves on-site sale and consumption of beer and wine within
an existing bona fide restaurant.
Summary:

The proposed project complies with all applicable regulations and, as conditioned, will not be
detrimental to the public health, safety, and welfare of surrounding uses. The request for approval
of the sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption (Type 41 ABC license) will create a more vibrant
commercial center and promote the economic viability of the existing restaurant. The alcohol service
will be ancillary to the existing bona fide restaurant and limited to hours of operation that will not
negatively impact the community. The project is consistent with the General Plan vision of providing
 Norwalk Planning Commission  May 14, 2025
  Page No. 5

adequate local-serving commercial uses. Staff recommends approval of the proposed project
subject to the conditions of approval.

   ATTACHMENT A
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  RESOLUTION NO. 25-07

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST
  NO. 2025-04 FOR ANCILLARY ON-SITE SALE AND CONSUMPTION OF
  BEER AND WINE (TYPE 41 ABC LICENSE) IN CONJUNCTION WITH AN
  EXISTING BONA FIDE RESTAURANT LOCATED AT 12227 NORWALK
  BOULEVARD WITHIN THE C-3 ZONE AND THE ADOPTION OF A CEQA
  CATEGORIAL EXEMPTION

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission for the City of Norwalk (“Planning Commission”)
has received Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2025-04, a request from Robert Drieslein, on
behalf of Norwalk Taco Factory (“Applicant”), for 12227 Norwalk Boulevard (“Subject Site”), a
request to approve as an ancillary use the on-site sale and consumption of beer and wine under
a Type 41 State Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) license within in an existing
1,400 square foot bona fide restaurant located within a 1.39-acre commercial shopping center
(the “Proposed Use”); and

  WHEREAS, the Subject Site is located at 12227 Norwalk Boulevard (APN: 8024-024-
023); and

  WHEREAS, the Subject Site is located within the C-3 (General Commercial) zoning
district; and

  WHEREAS, the Subject Site is designated as General Commercial by the General Plan;
and

  WHEREAS, Section 17.02.203 of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the
review and approval of a DAR by the Director of Community Development (“Director”) for the on-
sale alcohol sales within bona fide restaurants, and allows the Director to refer any request to the
Planning Commission for review; and

  WHEREAS, the Director has referred DAR No. 2025-04 to the Planning Commission for
review; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public hearing on May
14, 2025, to consider DAR No. 2025-04, at which time oral and documentary evidence relative to
the application were received.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

  Section 1. Environmental. The Proposed Use will not have a significant effect on the
environment per Section 15301 (Existing Facilities) of the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA), which consists of operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing or minor
alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical
features, involving negligible or no expansion of use beyond that existing at the time.

  Section 2. General Plan and Zoning. The subject property is located in the General
Commercial (C-3) zone and the proposed ancillary sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption

Resolution No. 25-07  Page 1 of 6
 is an added service is ancillary to the bona fide restaurant use. The Proposed Use will comply
with the zoning code and be consistent with General Plan objectives and policies for providing
adequate local-serving commercial uses, services supporting economic growth, and establishing
a positive image for Norwalk.

  Section 3. Planning Commission hereby finds and determines that the degree of
compatibility required by the Zoning Ordinance will be maintained with respect to the use of the
site, giving consideration to other existing and potential uses within the general area. The sale
and consumption of beer and wine within an existing bona fide restaurant is not anticipated to
significantly impact surrounding uses in the area with the incorporation of recommended
conditions of approval. The ancillary on-site alcohol service and consumption will occur within the
indoor dining area. The bona fide restaurant operations with ancillary on-site alcohol sales (Type
41 ABC License) will adhere to the Department of Public Safety’s Business Watch program and
complete Responsible Beverage Server training.

  Section 4. The Proposed Use will not be detrimental to the public health, safety, and
welfare of the community as it will be ancillary to the permitted bona fide restaurant within the
shopping center. Ancillary on-site alcohol service and consumption will occur within the indoor
dining area.

  Section 5. The sale and consumption of beer and wine in conjunction with an existing
bona fide restaurant will generate economic growth and revenue for the business. The bona fide
restaurant with ancillary beer and wine sales will serve the neighborhood and surrounding
community, positively upgrading the overall aesthetic character and ambiance. The Proposed
Use will result in an increase in business taxes in the City.

  Section 6. Finding of Public Convenience and Necessity will be required for the request
to allow the ancillary sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption (Type 41 ABC license) at the
Subject Site because it will exceed the existing concentration at four (4) establishments approved
for on-premise consumption. The bona fide restaurant with the on-sale license will serve the
neighborhood and surrounding community and will create a more vibrant commercial center and
promote the economic viability of the existing restaurant. The necessary finding for public
convenience and necessity can be made in a positive manner and is as follows:

  A. The finding of Public Convenience or Necessity (e.g. increases in employment, increases
  in business taxes, whether the Proposed Use is a unique business addition to the
  community, whether the Proposed Use will contribute to the economic goals of the area,
  and whether the Proposed Use will result in a positive upgrade of the area).

  Finding of Fact:

According to ABC, Census Tract No. 5553 has already reached the maximum allowable
recommended number of licenses allotted in the census tract. The maximum number of on-sale
licenses allowed is four (4) and there are currently six (6) on-sale licenses within the census tract.
Therefore, approval of this request would result in a total of seven (7) on-sale licenses further
contributing to the overconcentration of ABC licenses. Thus, a finding of Public Convenience or
Necessity must be made by the governing body in order to obtain the requested alcohol license
from ABC.

Staff finds that the Proposed Use can be supported with a finding of “Public Convenience”. The
addition of the sale of beer and wine for on-site consumption will is generally an expected offering

site alcohol sales are common ancillary use within a bona fide restaurant and will not directly or

request for a Type 41 ABC license will create a more vibrant commercial center and promote the
economic viability of the existing restaurant. Conditions of approval will be imposed on the
Proposed Use’s approval to ensure orderly commerce, business operations, and public safety.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION: To allow the on-site sale and consumption of beer and wine
(ABC Type 41 license) within an existing 1,400 square foot bona fide restaurant located
within an approximately 1.39-acre commercial shopping center.

The following is a list of code requirements deemed applicable to the proposed project based
on plans stated above. The list is intended to assist the applicant by identifying requirements,
which must be satisfied during the various stages of project permitting and implementation.
A list of conditions of approval adopted by the Planning Commission in conjunction with the
requested entitlement(s), if any, will also be provided upon final project approval. If you have
any questions regarding these requirements, please contact the Plan Reviewer.

  1. Development Standards and Operations - Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC) Section
  17.04.140.G.1):

  a. Alcohol must be served at tables or sit-down counters by employees of the
  restaurant and sold for on-site consumption.

  b. The sale of beer and wine for consumption off the premises is prohibited.

  c. Gross monthly sales of alcohol shall not exceed gross monthly sales of food
  and other non-alcohol items within the same period. The licensee shall at all
  times maintain records, which reflect separately the gross sale of food and the
  gross sales of alcoholic beverages of the licensed business. Said reports shall
  be kept no less frequently than on a quarterly basis and shall be made
  available to the City on demand.

  d. Entertainment in conjunction with the restaurant is limited to indoor ambient
  music to compliment the dining experience and shall be limited to background
  music at a low volume that is not audible outside of the building. The
   establishment shall remain in compliance with Title 9, Chapter 9.04, Article
  Ill.Noise.

  e. No employee or agent shall be permitted to accept money or any other thing
  of value from a customer for the purpose of sitting or otherwise spending time
  with customers while in the premises, nor shall the licensee/petitioner provide
  or permit, or make available either gratuitous or for compensation, male or
  female persons who act as escorts, companions, or guests of and for the
  customers.

  f. Licensee/petitioner shall not require an admission charge or a cover charge,
  nor shall there be a requirement to purchase a minimum number of drinks.

  g. The premises shall be maintained as a restaurant and shall provide a menu
  containing an assortment of food as offered in such restaurants.

  h. During normal meal hours, the business shall be designed and used for and
  must possess the necessary utensils, table service, and condiment dispensers
  with which to serve meals to the public.

  i.  Any graffiti painted or marked upon the premises shall be removed or painted
  over to match the color of the surface to which it is applied within forty-eight
  (48) hours of the discovery thereof.

  j.  Applicant will cooperate with the prosecution of offenders who engage in
  unlawful activity on site.

  k. The owner, manager, or person in charge of the establishment shall be twenty-
  one (21) years or older. At least one such person shall be present on the
  premises at all times. No person under the age of eighteen (18) shall sell or
  serve alcoholic beverages.

2. Security (NMC Section 17.04.140.G.2)

  a. Security lighting shall be provided on all sides of the exterior of the building
  and within the parking lot to fully illuminate all areas. All inoperable lighting
  shall be repaired/replaced within 24 hours to ensure adequate lighting is in
  place at all times. A lighting plan shall be submitted for review and approval
  by the Public Safety and Community Development Departments.

  b. The business operator shall participate in the Department of Public Safety's
  Business Watch program and anti-trespassing/enforcement program
  (S.H.A.P.E.), which includes signing of the Department SHAPE contract and
  Sheriff Letter of Agency, along with posting signage in the parking lot for "No
  Trespassing," and signage on the business front window/entrance area for "No
   Panhandling." Participation in the programs must be initiated within 30 days of
  obtaining Director approval.

  c. A surveillance camera system is to be maintained operational at all times,
  including during non-business hours. The system features and functions shall
  be accessible by business management staff at all times during normal
  business hours.

  d. A unique user ID and password shall be created and provided for the Public
  Safety Department to access the system at any time during an emergency or
  crime in progress. Business shall contact the Public Safety Department to
  provide this information within 30 days of the business starting operation.

  e. Business shall make all video stored on the digital video recording system
  available to the Public Safety Department and Norwalk Sheriff's Station at any
  time. The Public Safety and/or Sheriff's Station may request copies of
  recorded videos. Business must provide the requested video recording within
  24 hours of the Public Safety/Sheriff request.

  f. Cameras shall be placed to provide visual coverage of all entrances/exits,
  cash registers, safes, office/storage area, and adjacent parking areas. A
  security camera plan shall be submitted for review and approval by the Public
  Safety Department, Community Development Department, and the Norwalk
  Sheriff's Station.

3. Monitoring (NMC Section 17.04.140.G.3)

  a. The restaurant operator shall be responsible for maintaining the premises and
  adjoining rights-of-way free of debris and litter.

  b. The restaurant operator shall be responsible for monitoring both patron and
  employee conduct on the premises and within the parking areas under its
  control to prevent behavior that adversely affects or detracts from the quality
  of life for adjoining residents, property owners, and businesses.

  c. All trash and recycling bins under control of the restaurant operator shall be
  kept closed and locked at all times when they are not in use and shall be
  maintained such that they do not overflow.

  d. Loitering is prohibited on all areas under the control of the restaurant. A "No
  Loitering or Public Drinking" sign that is a minimum of four by six inches shall
  be posted outside next to every exit.

  e. A minimum of one on-duty manager with authority over the activities within the
  restaurant shall be on the premises at all times that the restaurant is open for
  business. The on-duty manager's responsibilities shall include the monitoring
   of the premises to ensure compliance with all applicable State laws, Municipal
  Code requirements and the conditions imposed by the Department of
  Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC). The restaurant shall be responsible for
  discouraging illegal and criminal activity on the subject premises and any
  exterior area under its control.

  f. All employees involved with the sale of alcohol are to complete a Responsible
  Beverage Server (RBS) training course approved by the California
  Department of Alcohol Beverage Control and City of Norwalk, Department of
  Public Safety within six months of Director Approval or an employee’s start
  date, whichever occurs later.

  g. Business manager and employees involved with the sale of alcohol, must
  attend the ABC Licensee Education on Alcohol and Drugs (LEAD) Program
  which is a free prevention and education program for retail licensees, and their
  employees. Program must be completed within six months of Director
  Approval or an employee’s start date, whichever occurs later.

  h. An electronic age verification device shall be retained on the premises
  available for use during operational hours. This device shall be maintained in
  operational condition and all employees shall be instructed in its use.

4. Administration (NMC Section 17.04.140.G.4)

  a. The owner or the operator of the bona fide restaurant shall request Director
  approval as prescribed in NMC Section 17.02.203.

  b. The applicant shall pay the fees required for Director Approval, as prescribed
  by a fee resolution adopted by the City Council.

  c. The City shall have the authority to conduct inspections to verify compliance
  with any and all of the requirements pursuant to NMC Section 17.04.140.G.

  d. The owner and operator shall execute and record a covenant and agreement
  satisfactory to the Director, acknowledging that the owner and operator shall
  agree to comply with each of the provisions set forth in this Section. A certified
  copy bearing the Recorder's number and date shall be provided to the
  Community Development Department, Planning Division. The agreement shall
  run with the land and shall be binding on any subsequent owners, heirs or
  assigns. The agreement with the requirements attached must be submitted to
  the Community Development Department, Planning Division for review and
  approval before being recorded.
